tonics.title: Glow
tonics.benefit: Turmeric and tamarind for skin that looks rested
tonics.ritual:
Stir one stick into 250 ml of cold water or sparkling water.
Add ice and a squeeze of lime.
Best in the morning, with or without food.
tonics.description: The most loved jamu in Java. Fresh turmeric root and tart tamarind, sweetened with a little palm sugar, as the mbok jamu still make it each morning in Solo.

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

tonics.title: Calm
tonics.benefit: Rice and aromatic ginger to wind down the evening
tonics.ritual:
Stir one stick into 250 ml of warm water or warm oat milk.
Sip slowly an hour before bed.
tonics.description: Toasted rice and kencur, a gentle, camphor-bright ginger. Soft, a little sweet, and the jamu Javanese grandmothers give children.

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

tonics.title: Digest
tonics.benefit: Javanese turmeric for an easier afternoon
tonics.ritual:
Stir one stick into 250 ml of hot water after lunch.
A slice of fresh ginger makes it sharper.
tonics.description: Temulawak is turmeric's bolder cousin, grown on the slopes of West Java. Earthy, slightly bitter, and traditionally taken after a heavy meal.

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

tonics.title: Warmth
tonics.benefit: Red ginger and cinnamon for cold mornings
tonics.ritual:
Stir one stick into 250 ml of hot water.
Add honey if you like it sweeter.
tonics.description: Red ginger is smaller and hotter than the common kind. We pair it with lemongrass and a little cinnamon for a drink that warms from the first sip.

items: Red ginger rhizome (Zingiber officinale var. rubrum)

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

tonics.title: Focus
tonics.benefit: Lemongrass and butterfly pea for clear afternoons
tonics.ritual:
Stir one stick into 250 ml of cold water. It turns deep blue.
Add lemon and watch it change to violet.
tonics.description: Butterfly pea flowers from Bali, dried in the sun, with fresh lemongrass. Bright, floral, caffeine-free, and it changes colour when you add citrus.

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

tonics.title: Energy
tonics.benefit: Moringa and pandan for a steady, caffeine-free lift
tonics.ritual:
Shake one stick with 250 ml of cold water or coconut water.
Good before a walk or a workout.
tonics.description: Moringa leaves from Madura, dried at low heat to keep their colour, with pandan for a soft vanilla note. Grassy, green and gently sweet.

footnotes: *Percent Daily Values are based on a 2,000 calorie diet.

ingredients.name: Turmeric
ingredients.story:
Kunyit is the backbone of jamu. Our growers in Karanganyar lift the rhizomes after the plant's leaves yellow, wash them in spring water and slice them thin to dry in the sun for four days.
Fresh turmeric is used in almost every Javanese kitchen, from curries to the yellow rice cooked for celebrations.

ingredients.name: Tamarind
ingredients.story:
Tamarind trees line the old roads of East Java. The sticky pulp gives kunyit asam its sourness, balancing the earthiness of turmeric.
We buy from a women's cooperative in Pasuruan that hand-shells every pod.

ingredients.name: Aromatic ginger
ingredients.story: Kencur is a small, low-growing ginger with a camphor-bright smell. It's the defining flavour of beras kencur and a common remedy for a sore throat.

ingredients.name: Rice
ingredients.story: We toast heirloom red and white rice from Jatiluwih's terraces until it smells like popcorn, then mill it fine. It gives beras kencur its body.

ingredients.name: Javanese turmeric
ingredients.story: Temulawak grows wild on the forest edges around Bogor. Larger and more bitter than common turmeric, it has been taken after meals in Java for centuries.

ingredients.name: Red ginger
ingredients.story: Red ginger has smaller rhizomes with a pink skin and much more heat than the yellow kind. Farmers in Boyolali plant it between rows of chilli.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.story: Grown in the same family gardens as the butterfly pea, lemongrass is cut every few weeks and dried in the shade so it keeps its oils.

ingredients.name: Butterfly pea
ingredients.story: The deep blue flowers climb fences across Bali. Picked each morning and dried in the sun, they colour rice cakes, teas and our Focus blend. Add citrus and the blue turns violet.

ingredients.name: Moringa
ingredients.story: Kelor grows fast in Madura's dry soil. Leaves are stripped by hand and dried below 40°C to keep their green colour.

ingredients.name: Pandan
ingredients.story: Pandan gives Indonesian sweets their soft, vanilla-like smell. A few leaves knotted into the rice pot is how most Balinese cooks use it.

accessory.title: Ritual Glass
accessory.description: A thick, short tumbler made by a family glassworks in Yogyakarta from recycled bottles. Each one has small bubbles, and no two are the same.
